body.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\), \((g,r)=(0,1)\), and \(P_W\in\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lift}}\), derive a finite similarity-invariant observable stratification that determines whether \(\{\pi^0_{0,1}(J):J\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}\}\subseteq\Delta^3\) is a singleton. The stratification must separate the HDK branch from every forecast-degenerate branch on which HDK fails but the target remains constant, list explicit polynomial or rational invariants and their degrees, and enumerate every positive legal-fiber component. For rational fixed-chart input, give a terminating algorithm and prove a bit-complexity bound polynomial in the coefficient bit length for this fixed stratum, hence strictly sharper than generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition or quantifier elimination.
body.justification: The sufficiency theorem and generic converse leave a non-generic, fixed one-alias-block boundary whose observable branch structure is unknown.
body.gap: Generic semialgebraic decidability and equality over legal lifts merely restate the problem. No located result supplies explicit invariants, degrees, component enumeration, and a fixed-dimension bit bound for this target-active stopped-HMM stratum.
body.consumer: The stratification would convert HDK rejection into a complete \(K=3\), binary, six-date diagnostic for the first future cohort forecast and would retain forecast-degenerate cases where the target is nevertheless identified.

obligation.what_is_open: The complete bivariate rational invariant list with degrees, the enumeration of every positive legal-fiber component on the forecast-degenerate HDK-failure locus, and a terminating fixed-stratum algorithm with coefficient-bit complexity polynomial in the input bit length.
obligation.obstruction: The corrected handle exposes a genuinely two-dimensional positive legal region. The frozen core contains neither its cleared bivariate target numerators nor a subresultant decomposition and Sturm--Habicht sign table for all forecast-degenerate branches. HDK sufficiency, the generic one-direction derivative, and the new rank-two hazard Jacobian do not decide higher-order or global target constancy on those exceptional components. Invoking generic quantifier elimination would not supply the requested explicit invariants or the promised sharper fixed-stratum bound.
obligation.attempted: Kept the full \(S(a,b)\) centralizer, computed its transformed-hazard coordinates and the nonzero Jacobian minor, proved that strict legality leaves a two-dimensional local region, reused HDK sufficiency, and used the alias-preserving derivative to settle unequal-hazard, unequal-forecast points. No univariate reduction was assumed without a proved elimination.
obligation.partial_result:
On the HDK branch, the established hazard-lift theorem gives the unique \(L\in\mathcal A_O\) satisfying \(L\bar v=\bar h\), so \(\{\pi^0_{0,1}(J):J\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}\}\) is a singleton. On the full alias-block centralizer
\[
 S(a,b)=\begin{pmatrix}a&1-a\\b&1-b\end{pmatrix},\qquad a\ne b,
\]
the transformed-hazard map has the certified Jacobian minor
\[
 -\frac{(h_1-h_2)^2}{(a-b)^4}.
\]
Hence unequal hazards give two locally independent hazard-lift directions at every strictly positive legal point; the strict legality inequalities do not collapse the local parameter dimension. Along the explicit alias-preserving direction used in the generic converse, unequal one-step forecasts give
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\mu^0_{0,1}(t)\right|_{t=0}
 =\frac{\alpha_i(h_j-h_i)\{(Pe)_j-(Pe)_i\}}{(1-h_i)p_0}\ne0,
\]
so the target fiber is not a singleton at every unequal-hazard, unequal-forecast point covered by that direction. What remains is the forecast-degenerate HDK-failure locus: its bivariate rational target numerators and positive legal-region components have not been explicitly enumerated, and no univariate reduction or fixed-coefficient-bit-complexity bound has yet been proved.
